title: Rockenfeller wins at Brands Hatch from inherited pole as Farfus stops
dek: Mike Rockenfeller led all 98 laps at Brands Hatch for Audi, 7.641 seconds clear of Bruno Spengler, after Martin Tomczyk lost pole for his underweight BMW and Augusto Farfus stopped from second.

chapters.title: Britain next for the Hockenheim winners
text: Two weeks after the Hockenheim opener the DTM made its only visit to Britain, with Brands Hatch hosting round two on Sunday 19 May. Augusto Farfus arrived at the head of the standings on 25 points after winning from second on the grid, with Schnitzer's Dirk Werner on 18 after climbing from 20th to second, and Christian Vietoris third on 15. The short 1.929-kilometre Indy circuit made overtaking difficult even with DRS and option tyres, and three drivers, Martin Tomczyk, Mike Rockenfeller and Farfus, were due to fly straight from the race to the Nürburgring 24 Hours.

chapters.title: Tomczyk takes pole, then loses it
text: On Saturday Tomczyk produced a lap of 41.158 seconds in the shootout for what looked like his first pole in a BMW. Rockenfeller was 0.035 seconds slower in the Phoenix Audi and Farfus 0.039 behind in third, while Joey Hand opened the shootout with a 41.460 and took fourth, the best qualifying result of his DTM career. Spengler missed the top-four session by about a hundredth of a second and was fifth ahead of Timo Scheider and Marco Wittmann, with Andy Priaulx, Edoardo Mortara and Miguel Molina completing the top ten.

It was a miserable session for Mercedes, which had no car in the top ten. Gary Paffett was only 12th. Jamie Green, in his first home race for Audi, started his final Q1 lap a tenth of a second after the flag and had the time deleted, which left him 18th, and Vietoris and Wehrlein also fell in Q1.

After qualifying the stewards found that Tomczyk's car was underweight. He was sent to the back of the grid and Rockenfeller inherited pole, with Farfus alongside him, Hand third and Spengler fourth, while Paffett moved up to 11th and Tomczyk started 22nd.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller gets away, Merhi makes enemies
text: Rockenfeller made a good start and held the lead from Farfus into the first corner. Spengler moved up to third, Wittmann gained two places from sixth, and Hand, who got away badly, dropped from third to sixth. Rockenfeller built a small lead on the option tyres in the early laps and was never in danger.

Behind them, there was trouble. Early in the race Roberto Merhi in the HWA Mercedes forced Glock onto the grass at the bottom of Graham Hill Bend, and at the same spot he later put Tomczyk, who was climbing through the field from the back, onto the grass as well. Both BMW drivers were angry afterwards, and Tomczyk finished 13th and Glock 14th, both out of the points.

chapters.title: Strategy gambles and a failure for Farfus
text: Each car had to make two stops. Paffett and his team made a gamble on the starting tyre, running standard, then option, then standard again, and it paid off, taking him from 11th on the grid into the podium positions. Wickens, who started 13th, made up places with the help of the options at the start, and HWA held him behind Paffett.

Farfus had run second for most of the race and was heading for another podium when a technical failure ended his afternoon after his second stop and left him stranded, 65 laps in. It cost him the points and the lead of the championship. Spengler, who had been running third, moved into second and stayed there to the flag.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller rules, Wickens gets lucky
text: Rockenfeller took the flag after 98 laps in 1:11:28.719, 7.641 seconds ahead of Spengler. The winner had controlled the race from the start. Spengler said Rockenfeller was quicker early on and he quicker at the end, but not by enough to pass. Paffett crossed the line third, but was given a five-second penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags and dropped to sixth, which handed the final podium place to Wickens, 24.368 seconds behind, who thereby took his first DTM podium.

Wittmann was fourth, 24.964 seconds back, and Hand fifth, with Paffett sixth after the penalty. Ekström climbed from 12th to seventh, ahead of Vietoris, Scheider and Wehrlein, who took the last point in tenth. Paffett also set the fastest lap, a 42.124 on lap six. Werner recovered only to 12th from 14th on the grid, and Mortara was classified 21st, eleven laps down.

chapters.title: Audi takes the lead of the championship
text: Rockenfeller said he had controlled the race from the start, that his Audi had worked perfectly and that both stops had gone well, and that the option tyres had not lasted as well as expected, which he thought was the case for everyone. Audi's DTM head Dieter Gass said the win was a confirmation of the winter's work and that Rockenfeller had dominated for 98 laps without a mistake, while Audi motorsport chief Wolfgang Ullrich pointed out that such dominant victories are rare in the DTM. Ernst Moser, team principal of Phoenix, said the celebrations would have to wait because the team was still involved at the Nürburgring 24 Hours.

BMW was content with a second place, said motorsport director Jens Marquardt, and with three cars in the top five, though six cars in the top ten on the grid might have meant more. Spengler said the pace had been good and the strategy perfect, and he was happy to get on the podium. Wittmann, in only his second DTM race, took fourth, and Hand fifth, though Hand said his start had gone wrong and the car had podium potential. For Farfus the retirement from second place was the day's big disappointment, and Glock and Tomczyk were both openly critical of Merhi after being forced off by the Mercedes driver.

Mercedes motorsport chief Toto Wolff said Sunday had been much better than Saturday, with four cars in the top ten, and that luck had played its part. Wickens could hardly believe his first podium, which he called a miracle, crediting a strong start on the new option tyres and two good stops, while Wehrlein scored his first point in tenth. With Audi, BMW and Mercedes all represented on the podium, Wolff called it good for the series.

The result changed the championship. Rockenfeller led with 29 points after his win, one ahead of Spengler on 28, with Farfus third on 25. Paffett was fourth with 20, Vietoris fifth with 19 and Werner sixth with 18. The DTM would next race in Spielberg, Austria, on 2 June, but Rockenfeller, Tomczyk and Farfus had the Nürburgring 24 Hours to get through first.

facts.v: Martin Tomczyk lost his 41.158 pole after the stewards found his BMW underweight and started 22nd, so Rockenfeller started from pole.
